title: UMAP analysis of DESI spectra surfaces newly recognized inhomogeneous white dwarfs
summary: A machine-learning-guided analysis of DESI multi-epoch spectra used UMAP to identify three systems with strongly varying spectral signatures that were proposed as new ‘double-faced’ white dwarfs with inhomogeneous surface composition. Follow-up phase-resolved time-series spectra verified the interpretation for one system; the other two remain candidates. This is one paper-level result and only the verified system is counted as confirmed.
ai_technology: UMAP dimensionality reduction applied to multi-epoch white-dwarf spectroscopy, alongside a neural-network spectral classifier
organization: University of Warwick; University of Leicester; University of Barcelona; Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias; DESI collaboration

evidence.tested: A machine-learning-guided analysis of DESI multi-epoch spectra used UMAP to identify three systems with strongly varying spectral signatures that were proposed as new ‘double-faced’ white dwarfs with inhomogeneous surface composition.
evidence.unknown: The paper describes three new candidates, but only one has validating phase-resolved time-series spectra; the remaining two have limited/unequal signal-to-noise and are not included as confirmed objects. Existing classification of the first source as a DA+DB binary was challenged, not assumed disproven without the authors’ supporting phase-dependent evidence.
evidence.ai_role: Mapped spectral/photometric features and flagged white dwarfs with strongly changing multi-epoch spectra for expert review; this identified the systems subsequently investigated with phase-resolved spectroscopy.
